relationships.subject: paclitaxel
relationships.evidence_quote: systemic paclitaxel administration upregulates the expression of neurotrophin-3 (Nt3) mRNA and its encoded proneurotrophin-3 (proNT3) protein in the neurons of dorsal root ganglia (DRG), but not in the spinal cord.

relationships.subject: proNT3
relationships.evidence_quote: Conversely, mimicking paclitaxel-induced upregulation of DRG proNT3 produces enhanced responses to mechanical, heat, and cold stimuli and spontaneous pain in naive male and female mice.

relationships.subject: proNT3
relationships.evidence_quote: Mechanistically, proNT3 triggers tropomyosin receptor kinase C (TrkC) activation and participates in the paclitaxel-induced increases of C-C chemokine ligand 2 (Ccl2) mRNA and CCL2 protein in the DRG.

relationships.subject: proNT3
relationships.evidence_quote: Mechanistically, proNT3 triggers tropomyosin receptor kinase C (TrkC) activation and participates in the paclitaxel-induced increases of C-C chemokine ligand 2 (Ccl2) mRNA and CCL2 protein in the DRG.

relationships.subject: proNT3
relationships.evidence_quote: This microinjection also led to stimulation-independent spontaneous pain and increased neuronal and astrocyte activities in the ipsilateral L3/4 dorsal horn 8 weeks after viral microinjection (Fig. 6G–I).

key_findings: Paclitaxel upregulates proNT3 (not mature NT3) in DRG neurons; knockdown attenuates paclitaxel-induced hypersensitivity and spontaneous pain in both sexes.
DRG proNT3 overexpression alone produces pain hypersensitivity, acting through TrkC to elevate CCL2.
